meta.score: score = 100/(1 + d/d50); d = median, over the target tiles, of the distance to the most similar tile of the place, with EQUAL WEIGHT PER GROUP (terrain, land cover, temperature, geology): d = root mean square of the group distances. Numeric groups: RMS of standardized differences (log1p + z-score); geology: 0 same class, 0.5 undefined, 1 different. d50 = median of all target→place distances. 50 = typical pair, 100 = identical.
meta.dist_grupos: how far each group sets the place apart from the target (0 = equal); explains the score
meta.contribuicao: standardized difference (place − target) of each feature in the most similar pair of tiles; near 0 = similar in that feature.
meta.coordenadas: Earth: WGS84. Moon/Mars: planetocentric in the body spherical CRS. East-positive longitude in -180..180.

avisos: Similarity covers terrain, land cover, surface temperature and geology (a harmonized rock class, which is an interpretation of regional maps).
Temperatures come from sources of different kinds (reanalysis on Earth, a model fitted to Diviner on the Moon, a climate model on Mars): comparable in order of magnitude, not within a few kelvin.
Moon and Mars: land cover is assigned (bare ground = 1), not measured.
Flat places on Earth measured with NASADEM look steeper/rougher than they are (DEM noise).
Lunar region centers: PGDA DEMs with the same name (matched by name, not official). Mars: landing points checked; Oxia at the IAU name center.
Antarctica: land cover from the AADC rock outcrop map (100 m), which does not separate ice from sea.
The Earth places were chosen by the team (mostly known analogs): the ranking orders this list; it is not a search of the whole planet.
The method finds terrain and environment analogs; mineralogical/astrobiological analogs (e.g. Rio Tinto) rank low because mineral composition is not measured.
The ranking is the similarity score (explained by group); the ZEUS clusters are a complementary view.

clima_marte.fonte: Luís Gustavo de Oliveira Miranda — Análogos climáticos de Marte na Terra (2026-11-14)
clima_marte.metodo: Gower, 9 grandezas, pesos 0,5 nas 6 térmicas; pressão log10; precipitação log(1+x)
avisos: Mars is model output (2° cell, ~120 km, a regional mean), not measurement; Earth is a single year of daily data (Meteomatics, through Nov 2026), not a climatology.

No place on Earth comes close to Mars in pressure (the lowest on Earth is ~31 times the highest on Mars) or in day–night change: the values point to the "least different" place, not an equivalent climate.
Climate barely separates one Mars target from another: the most similar places are almost the same for all six.

Gower similarity depends on the range of values in the analyzed set (507 Earth points + 16,200 Mars cells). It is kept out of the main score because it works at another scale (~120 km region × 9 km tiles).
Dust on Earth = optical depth of mineral dust only (dust AOD 550 nm); the original report used total AOD, which includes pollution.
